titleEn: An empty taxi is coming towards us

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book gloss: more and more; increasingly. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 越来越 like the word 田芳 uses when the bus queue keeps growing — 等车的人越来越多了 — and you’d rather 打的.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 越来越 + adj./verb to mark a change over time. Don’t stack another degree adverb after it.

example.zh: 等车的人越来越多了，咱们还是打的去吧，别坐公共汽车了。
example.pinyin: Děng chē de rén yuèláiyuè duō le, zánmen háishi dǎ dī qù ba, bié zuò gōnggòngqìchē le.
example.en: More and more people are waiting for the bus — let’s take a taxi instead of the bus.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to take a taxi. Colloquial Beijing 的 = dī. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 打的 like 田芳’s fix when the bus stop is packed — skip the 公共汽车 and 打的去.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 打的 for hailing a taxi in casual talk. Formal writing may prefer 坐出租车.

example.zh: 等车的人越来越多了，咱们还是打的去吧，别坐公共汽车了。
example.pinyin: Děng chē de rén yuèláiyuè duō le, zánmen háishi dǎ dī qù ba, bié zuò gōnggòngqìchē le.
example.en: More and more people are waiting for the bus — let’s take a taxi instead of the bus.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) vacant; unoccupied. Tone kōng (not kòng ‘free time’). Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 空 like the empty taxi 玛丽 spots — 一辆空车 — so they can hop in right away.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 空 for an empty seat/vehicle: 空车, 空位. For spare time they use 空(kòng).

example.zh: 好吧，你看，那边正好开过来一辆空车，就坐这辆吧。
example.pinyin: Hǎo ba, nǐ kàn, nàbiān zhènghǎo kāi guòlái yí liàng kōng chē, jiù zuò zhè liàng ba.
example.en: Okay — look, an empty taxi is coming over; let’s take that one.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book lists 四合院(儿). Text uses 儿化. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 四合院儿 like 玛丽’s first question in the taxi — is 田芳’s home that traditional Beijing courtyard?
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 四合院儿 for the old courtyard house type; the note in this lesson explains the layout.

example.zh: 你家住的是四合院儿吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ jiā zhù de shì sìhéyuànr ma?
example.en: Does your family live in a siheyuan (courtyard house)?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) yard; courtyard. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 院子 like the open middle of 田芳’s home where the big date tree grows.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 院子 for the yard inside a compound, not the building itself.

example.zh: 是啊。我家院子里种着一棵大枣树，树上结着很多红枣，远远儿地就能看见。
example.pinyin: Shì a. Wǒ jiā yuànzi li zhòngzhe yì kē dà zǎoshù, shù shàng jiēzhe hěn duō hóngzǎo, yuǎnyuǎnr de jiù néng kànjian.
example.en: Yes. There’s a big jujube tree in our courtyard with lots of red dates — you can see it from far away.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to plant; to grow. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 种 like what sits in 田芳’s yard — 种着一棵大枣树 — planted and still there.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 种 for planting crops or trees. 种着 marks the ongoing planted state.

example.zh: 我家院子里种着一棵大枣树。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yuànzi li zhòngzhe yì kē dà zǎoshù.
example.en: There’s a big jujube tree planted in our courtyard.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (量) a measure word for plants, etc. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 棵 like the counter before 大枣树 — one whole tree, not 个.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers pair 棵 with trees and many plants: 一棵树.

example.zh: 我家院子里种着一棵大枣树。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yuànzi li zhòngzhe yì kē dà zǎoshù.
example.en: There’s a big jujube tree planted in our courtyard.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) jujube; (Chinese) date. Compounds in text: 枣树, 红枣. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 枣 like 田芳’s welcome snack — taste the family’s 红枣, they’re really sweet.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 红枣 for the fruit and 枣树 for the tree.

example.zh: 今天请你们尝尝我家的红枣，可甜了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān qǐng nǐmen chángchang wǒ jiā de hóngzǎo, kě tián le.
example.en: Today I’ll have you taste our family’s red dates — they’re so sweet.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to bear (fruit). Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 结 like the dates hanging on the tree — 树上结着很多红枣.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 结 for fruit forming on a plant: 结果, 结着红枣.

example.zh: 树上结着很多红枣，远远儿地就能看见。
example.pinyin: Shù shàng jiēzhe hěn duō hóngzǎo, yuǎnyuǎnr de jiù néng kànjian.
example.en: The tree is bearing lots of red dates; you can see them from far away.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to taste. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 尝 like 田芳 inviting guests to try the dates — 尝尝我家的红枣.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers reduplicate 尝尝 for a casual ‘have a taste.’

example.zh: 今天请你们尝尝我家的红枣，可甜了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān qǐng nǐmen chángchang wǒ jiā de hóngzǎo, kě tián le.
example.en: Today I’ll have you taste our family’s red dates — they’re so sweet.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) sweet. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 甜 like 田芳’s punchline about the dates — 可甜了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 甜 for taste; 可甜了 is strong colloquial emphasis.

example.zh: 今天请你们尝尝我家的红枣，可甜了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān qǐng nǐmen chángchang wǒ jiā de hóngzǎo, kě tián le.
example.en: Today I’ll have you taste our family’s red dates — they’re so sweet.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book pattern (no POS). Degree rises with a condition, not just time. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 越……越…… like 田芳 on the city changing — 大楼越盖越多, 小区也越建越漂亮.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers put a verb/adj after each 越. Don’t add 很/非常 after the second 越.

example.zh: 现在城市里大楼越盖越多，住宅小区也越建越漂亮。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài chéngshì li dàlóu yuè gài yuè duō, zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang.
example.en: Now more and more tall buildings are going up in the city, and housing compounds are being built more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to construct; to build. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 盖 like the boom 田芳 describes — 大楼越盖越多.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 盖 for putting up buildings. 盖房子 is the everyday collocation.

example.zh: 现在城市里大楼越盖越多，住宅小区也越建越漂亮。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài chéngshì li dàlóu yuè gài yuè duō, zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang.
example.en: Now more and more tall buildings are going up in the city, and housing compounds are being built more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) residence; dwelling. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 住宅 like the formal half of 住宅小区 — the housing estates replacing courtyards.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers keep 住宅 for residential buildings/areas, often in compounds like 住宅小区.

example.zh: 现在城市里大楼越盖越多，住宅小区也越建越漂亮。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài chéngshì li dàlóu yuè gài yuè duō, zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang.
example.en: Now more and more tall buildings are going up in the city, and housing compounds are being built more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) residential complex; housing estate. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 小区 like the modern housing blocks 田芳 says are 越建越漂亮.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 小区 for a gated/planned residential community.

example.zh: 住宅小区也越建越漂亮。
example.pinyin: Zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang.
example.en: The housing estates are also being built more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to build; to construct. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 建 like 小区越建越漂亮 — construction that keeps looking better.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 建 for constructing; close to 盖, often with larger projects.

example.zh: 住宅小区也越建越漂亮。
example.pinyin: Zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang.
example.en: The housing estates are also being built more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to move. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 搬 like neighbors leaving the courtyard — 搬走了五六家 — and 田芳’s family next year.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 搬家 / 搬走 for changing homes.

example.zh: 我们院子里最近也搬走了五六家，明年我们家也要搬走了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yuànzi li zuìjìn yě bānzǒu le wǔ liù jiā, míngnián wǒmen jiā yě yào bānzǒu le.
example.en: Five or six families in our courtyard have moved out recently; our family will move next year too.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) sorry; regretful. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 遗憾 like 玛丽’s reaction when she hears they’ll leave the little courtyard — 那太遗憾了.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 遗憾 for polite regret about a situation, not deep grief.

example.zh: 那太遗憾了。
example.pinyin: Nà tài yíhàn le.
example.en: That’s such a pity.

words.en: to be loath to part with; to grudge
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to be loath to use or part with; to grudge. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 舍不得 like 田芳 still loving the small yard even while hoping to move into a modern building.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 舍不得 for emotional reluctance to leave or spend something valued.

example.zh: 我虽然也舍不得离开我们家的小院儿，但还是希望快点儿搬进现代化的楼房里去住。
example.pinyin: Wǒ suīrán yě shěbude líkāi wǒmen jiā de xiǎo yuànr, dàn háishi xīwàng kuàidiǎnr bān jìn xiàndàihuà de lóufáng li qù zhù.
example.en: Although I’m reluctant to leave our little courtyard, I still hope to move into a modern apartment building soon.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to leave. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 离开 like what 田芳 can’t quite bear — 舍不得离开我们家的小院儿.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 离开 for departing a place or person.

example.zh: 我虽然也舍不得离开我们家的小院儿，但还是希望快点儿搬进现代化的楼房里去住。
example.pinyin: Wǒ suīrán yě shěbude líkāi wǒmen jiā de xiǎo yuànr, dàn háishi xīwàng kuàidiǎnr bān jìn xiàndàihuà de lóufáng li qù zhù.
example.en: Although I’m reluctant to leave our little courtyard, I still hope to move into a modern apartment building soon.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to modernize. In the 课文 it modifies 楼房 (‘modernized’). Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 现代化 like the apartments 田芳 still wants despite missing the courtyard.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 现代化 as verb or as 现代化的 + noun for modern facilities.

example.zh: 我虽然也舍不得离开我们家的小院儿，但还是希望快点儿搬进现代化的楼房里去住。
example.pinyin: Wǒ suīrán yě shěbude líkāi wǒmen jiā de xiǎo yuànr, dàn háishi xīwàng kuàidiǎnr bān jìn xiàndàihuà de lóufáng li qù zhù.
example.en: Although I’m reluctant to leave our little courtyard, I still hope to move into a modern apartment building soon.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) casual; informal. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 随便 like 王老师 opening the class chat — 随便谈谈自己的感想和体会.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 随便谈/说 to invite informal talk, not ‘do as you please’ rudeness here.

example.zh: 今天，想请大家随便谈谈自己的感想和体会，有什么意见和建议也可以提。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān, xiǎng qǐng dàjiā suíbiàn tántan zìjǐ de gǎnxiǎng hé tǐhuì, yǒu shénme yìjiàn hé jiànyì yě kěyǐ tí.
example.en: Today I’d like everyone to casually share your impressions and experiences; you can also raise any opinions or suggestions.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) impressions; thoughts. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 感想 like what 王老师 asks students to share after two months of Chinese.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 感想 for reflective impressions after an experience.

example.zh: 今天，想请大家随便谈谈自己的感想和体会。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān, xiǎng qǐng dàjiā suíbiàn tántan zìjǐ de gǎnxiǎng hé tǐhuì.
example.en: Today I’d like everyone to casually share your impressions and experiences.

words.en: to know from experience; understanding; feeling
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动、名) to know from experience; understanding; feeling. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 体会 like the lived side of class feedback — paired with 感想 in 王老师’s prompt.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 体会 for insight gained by living through something.

example.zh: 今天，想请大家随便谈谈自己的感想和体会。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān, xiǎng qǐng dàjiā suíbiàn tántan zìjǐ de gǎnxiǎng hé tǐhuì.
example.en: Today I’d like everyone to casually share your impressions and experiences.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) opinion; complaint. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 意见 like feedback 王老师 welcomes — 有什么意见和建议也可以提.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 意见 for opinions or critiques offered to improve something.

example.zh: 有什么意见和建议也可以提。
example.pinyin: Yǒu shénme yìjiàn hé jiànyì yě kěyǐ tí.
example.en: You can also raise any opinions or suggestions.

words.en: advice; suggestion; to advise; to suggest
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名、动) advice; suggestion; to advise; to suggest. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 建议 like 麦克 closing class talk — 我建议，咱们开一个新年联欢会.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers follow 建议 with a concrete plan. As a noun it pairs with 提建议.

example.zh: 老师，我建议，咱们开一个新年联欢会，怎么样？
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ jiànyì, zánmen kāi yí ge xīnnián liánhuānhuì, zěnmeyàng?
example.en: Teacher, I suggest we hold a New Year party — how about it?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to raise; to bring up. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 提 like 王老师’s invite — opinions and suggestions 也可以提.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 提 for bringing up a topic, opinion, or request.

example.zh: 有什么意见和建议也可以提。
example.pinyin: Yǒu shénme yìjiàn hé jiànyì yě kěyǐ tí.
example.en: You can also raise any opinions or suggestions.

words.en: to go out; to leave home
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to go out; to leave home. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 出门 like the proverb 麦克 quotes — 出门靠朋友.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 出门 for leaving home / being away from family.

example.zh: 朋友越多越好，“在家靠父母，出门靠朋友”嘛。
example.pinyin: Péngyou yuè duō yuè hǎo, “zài jiā kào fùmǔ, chū mén kào péngyou” ma.
example.en: The more friends the better — ‘at home rely on parents; away from home rely on friends.’

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) people. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 人们 like 麦克 talking about daily life getting richer — 人们的生活一天比一天丰富.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 人们 for people in general, not a specific group of named persons.

example.zh: 我觉得人们的生活一天比一天丰富，年轻人越来越会打扮，打扮得越来越漂亮了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde rénmen de shēnghuó yì tiān bǐ yì tiān fēngfù, niánqīngrén yuèláiyuè huì dǎban, dǎban de yuèláiyuè piàoliang le.
example.en: I feel people’s lives are getting richer day by day; young people are better and better at dressing up, and they’re dressing more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) rich; plentiful. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 丰富 like 麦克’s line on life getting fuller — 一天比一天丰富.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 丰富 for plentiful content/experience, not only money.

example.zh: 我觉得人们的生活一天比一天丰富。
example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde rénmen de shēnghuó yì tiān bǐ yì tiān fēngfù.
example.en: I feel people’s lives are getting richer day by day.

words.en: to dress up; to make up
words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to dress up; to make up. Neutral tone on ban. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 打扮 like 麦克’s title line — young people 越来越会打扮.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 打扮 for grooming/dressing up; 打扮得 + adj. is a state complement.

example.zh: 年轻人越来越会打扮，打扮得越来越漂亮了。
example.pinyin: Niánqīngrén yuèláiyuè huì dǎban, dǎban de yuèláiyuè piàoliang le.
example.en: Young people are better and better at dressing up, and they’re dressing more and more beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) new year; New Year’s Day. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 新年 like the season with Christmas — 圣诞节和新年快到了 — and 麦克’s 新年联欢会 idea.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 新年 for the New Year period; China’s biggest festival is still 春节.

example.zh: 圣诞节和新年快到了，不少商店都摆着圣诞树，装饰得非常漂亮。
example.pinyin: Shèngdàn Jié hé xīnnián kuài dào le, bù shǎo shāngdiàn dōu bǎizhe shèngdànshù, zhuāngshì de fēicháng piàoliang.
example.en: Christmas and New Year are almost here; quite a few shops have Christmas trees on display, decorated very beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) Christmas tree. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 圣诞树 like what 玛丽 sees in shops — and Chinese people buying them too.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 圣诞树 for the decorated tree associated with Christmas.

example.zh: 不少商店都摆着圣诞树，装饰得非常漂亮，我看见很多中国人也买圣诞树和圣诞礼物。
example.pinyin: Bù shǎo shāngdiàn dōu bǎizhe shèngdànshù, zhuāngshì de fēicháng piàoliang, wǒ kànjian hěn duō Zhōngguó rén yě mǎi shèngdànshù hé shèngdàn lǐwù.
example.en: Quite a few shops have Christmas trees on display, decorated very beautifully; I’ve seen many Chinese people buying Christmas trees and Christmas gifts too.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动、名) to decorate; decoration. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 装饰 like how the shop trees look — 装饰得非常漂亮.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 装饰 as verb with 得-complements, or as a noun for décor.

example.zh: 不少商店都摆着圣诞树，装饰得非常漂亮。
example.pinyin: Bù shǎo shāngdiàn dōu bǎizhe shèngdànshù, zhuāngshì de fēicháng piàoliang.
example.en: Quite a few shops have Christmas trees on display, decorated very beautifully.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) present; gift. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 礼物 like kids getting presents from parents — and 圣诞礼物 in the shops.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 礼物 for gifts in general; 圣诞礼物 is the Christmas set.

example.zh: 孩子们能从爸爸妈妈那儿得到礼物，当然也很高兴。
example.pinyin: Háizimen néng cóng bàba māma nàr dédào lǐwù, dāngrán yě hěn gāoxìng.
example.en: Kids can get presents from their parents, so of course they’re happy too.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (形) happy; joyous. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 欢乐 like the Christmas atmosphere 王老师 names — 欢乐的气氛.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 欢乐 for a festive, joyful mood, often with 气氛.

example.zh: 有的人过圣诞节，可能是喜欢圣诞节那种欢乐的气氛。
example.pinyin: Yǒu de rén guò Shèngdàn Jié, kěnéng shì xǐhuan Shèngdàn Jié nà zhǒng huānlè de qìfēn.
example.en: Some people celebrate Christmas, maybe because they like that joyous Christmas atmosphere.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) festival; holiday. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 节日 like 王老师’s punchline — China’s biggest 节日 is still 春节.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 节日 for festivals and public holidays.

example.zh: 不过，中国最大的节日还是春节。
example.pinyin: Búguò, Zhōngguó zuì dà de jiérì háishi Chūnjié.
example.en: But China’s biggest festival is still Spring Festival.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (动) to hold (a meeting, symposium, etc.) — this lesson’s sense, not ‘to open.’ Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 开 like 麦克’s suggestion — 开一个新年联欢会.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 开 + meeting/party nouns: 开会, 开联欢会.

example.zh: 老师，我建议，咱们开一个新年联欢会，怎么样？
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ jiànyì, zánmen kāi yí ge xīnnián liánhuānhuì, zěnmeyàng?
example.en: Teacher, I suggest we hold a New Year party — how about it?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. Book: (名) get-together; party. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 联欢会 like the New Year party 麦克 proposes and 王老师 accepts with 好啊!
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 联欢会 for a festive group gathering, often school/company.

example.zh: 老师，我建议，咱们开一个新年联欢会，怎么样？
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ jiànyì, zánmen kāi yí ge xīnnián liánhuānhuì, zěnmeyàng?
example.en: Teacher, I suggest we hold a New Year party — how about it?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. 专名. Book also lists 圣诞 Shèngdàn. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 圣诞节 like the holiday 玛丽 and 麦克 ask about — and 王老师 says most families don’t celebrate it.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 圣诞节 for the holiday; 圣诞 alone appears in compounds like 圣诞树.

example.zh: 老师，我听说中国过圣诞节的人越来越多了，是吗？
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ tīngshuō Zhōngguó guò Shèngdàn Jié de rén yuèláiyuè duō le, shì ma?
example.en: Teacher, I heard more and more people in China celebrate Christmas — is that true?

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. 专名, listed under 圣诞节 in the book. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 圣诞 like the short form inside 圣诞树 and 圣诞礼物 in 玛丽’s shopping talk.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers keep 圣诞 in compounds; the full holiday name is 圣诞节.

example.zh: 我看见很多中国人也买圣诞树和圣诞礼物。
example.pinyin: Wǒ kànjian hěn duō Zhōngguó rén yě mǎi shèngdànshù hé shèngdàn lǐwù.
example.en: I’ve seen many Chinese people buying Christmas trees and Christmas gifts too.

words.note: Headword pinyin printed in the book. 专名. Book: first day of the first lunar month. Example-sentence / dialogue-line pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 春节 like 王老师’s contrast — even if some celebrate Christmas, China’s biggest festival is 春节.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers treat 春节 as the main traditional New Year festival.

example.zh: 不过，中国最大的节日还是春节。
example.pinyin: Búguò, Zhōngguó zuì dà de jiérì háishi Chūnjié.
example.en: But China’s biggest festival is still Spring Festival.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added. Book prints zuò kè.
words.when: Remember 做客 like visiting someone's home as a guest — 到田芳家去做客.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 去做客 / 来做客 for a social home visit. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 昨天我们到田芳家去做客。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒmen dào Tián Fāng jiā qù zuòkè.
example.en: Yesterday we went to Tian Fang's house as guests.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 书房 like the room full of books you visit first — 我爸爸的书房.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a study / home library room. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 田芳说：“先参观参观我爸爸的书房吧。”
example.pinyin: Tián Fāng shuō: "Xiān cānguān cānguān wǒ bàba de shūfáng ba."
example.en: Tian Fang said, "First let's have a look at my dad's study."

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 文学 like the books on the shelf — 文学、历史方面的.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 文学 for literature as a field of study. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 书架里放着很多书，有中文的，也有外文的，有文学、历史方面的，也有政治、哲学方面的。
example.pinyin: Shūjià li fàngzhe hěn duō shū, yǒu Zhōngwén de, yě yǒu wàiwén de, yǒu wénxué, lìshǐ fāngmiàn de, yě yǒu zhèngzhì, zhéxué fāngmiàn de.
example.en: The bookshelves held many books — Chinese and foreign; literature and history, and also politics and philosophy.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 政治 like the shelf category next to 哲学 — 政治、哲学方面的.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 政治 for politics as a subject/field. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 书架里放着很多书，有中文的，也有外文的，有文学、历史方面的，也有政治、哲学方面的。
example.pinyin: Shūjià li fàngzhe hěn duō shū, yǒu Zhōngwén de, yě yǒu wàiwén de, yǒu wénxué, lìshǐ fāngmiàn de, yě yǒu zhèngzhì, zhéxué fāngmiàn de.
example.en: The bookshelves held many books — Chinese and foreign; literature and history, and also politics and philosophy.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 哲学 like the other shelf category next to 政治 — 政治、哲学方面的.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 哲学 for philosophy as a field. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 书架里放着很多书，有中文的，也有外文的，有文学、历史方面的，也有政治、哲学方面的。
example.pinyin: Shūjià li fàngzhe hěn duō shū, yǒu Zhōngwén de, yě yǒu wàiwén de, yǒu wénxué, lìshǐ fāngmiàn de, yě yǒu zhèngzhì, zhéxué fāngmiàn de.
example.en: The bookshelves held many books — Chinese and foreign; literature and history, and also politics and philosophy.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 写字台 like the desk by the window — 窗前是一张写字台.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a writing desk (often with drawers). From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 窗前是一张写字台，写字台旁边放着一台新电脑。
example.pinyin: Chuāng qián shì yì zhāng xiězìtái, xiězìtái pángbiān fàngzhe yì tái xīn diànnǎo.
example.en: In front of the window was a writing desk, and beside the desk was a new computer.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 沙发 like the living-room seating that frames the calligraphy — 沙发后面的墙上.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 沙发 for a sofa / couch. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 沙发后面的墙上挂着几幅字画。
example.pinyin: Shāfā hòumian de qiáng shàng guàzhe jǐ fú zìhuà.
example.en: On the wall behind the sofa hung several pieces of calligraphy and paintings.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 爷爷 like the grandfather who left the books and calligraphy — 我爷爷留给我们的.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 爷爷 for paternal grandfather. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 这些书和字画都是我爷爷留给我们的。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū hé zìhuà dōu shì wǒ yéye liú gěi wǒmen de.
example.en: These books and calligraphy pieces were all left to us by my grandpa.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 包 like wrapping dumplings — 包饺子.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers 包饺子 for making dumplings by hand. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 我们洗了手就开始包饺子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xǐ le shǒu jiù kāishǐ bāo jiǎozi.
example.en: We washed our hands and started wrapping dumplings.

words.note: 补充生词 (练习). Headword pinyin printed in the book. Example-sentence pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 老鼠 like Tian Fang's joke about a clumsy dumpling — 像小老鼠.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 老鼠 for mouse/rat; here it is a playful shape comparison. From lesson 16 综合填空 补充生词.

example.zh: 田芳说我包的饺子像小老鼠，说得大家都笑了。
example.pinyin: Tián Fāng shuō wǒ bāo de jiǎozi xiàng xiǎo lǎoshǔ, shuō de dàjiā dōu xiào le.
example.en: Tian Fang said the dumpling I wrapped looked like a little mouse, and everyone laughed.

dialogues.label: 课文（一）
dialogues.headingEn: An empty taxi is coming towards us

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 等车的人越来越多了，咱们还是打的去吧，别坐公共汽车了。
lines.pinyin: Děng chē de rén yuèláiyuè duō le, zánmen háishi dǎ dī qù ba, bié zuò gōnggòngqìchē le.
lines.en: More and more people are waiting for the bus — let’s take a taxi; don’t take the bus.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 好吧，你看，那边正好开过来一辆空车，就坐这辆吧。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo ba, nǐ kàn, nàbiān zhènghǎo kāi guòlái yí liàng kōng chē, jiù zuò zhè liàng ba.
lines.en: Okay — look, an empty taxi is coming over this way; let’s take that one.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 你家住的是四合院儿吗？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ jiā zhù de shì sìhéyuànr ma?
lines.en: Does your family live in a siheyuan?

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 是啊。我家院子里种着一棵大枣树，树上结着很多红枣，远远儿地就能看见。一看见那棵大枣树就看到我家了。今天请你们尝尝我家的红枣，可甜了。
lines.pinyin: Shì a. Wǒ jiā yuànzi li zhòngzhe yì kē dà zǎoshù, shù shàng jiēzhe hěn duō hóngzǎo, yuǎnyuǎnr de jiù néng kànjian. Yí kànjian nà kē dà zǎoshù jiù kàndào wǒ jiā le. Jīntiān qǐng nǐmen chángchang wǒ jiā de hóngzǎo, kě tián le.
lines.en: Yes. There’s a big jujube tree in our courtyard with lots of red dates — you can see it from far away. Once you see that tree, you’ve found our place. Today I’ll have you taste our red dates; they’re so sweet.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 我听说现在住四合院儿的越来越少了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ tīngshuō xiànzài zhù sìhéyuànr de yuèláiyuè shǎo le.
lines.en: I’ve heard fewer and fewer people live in siheyuan now.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 是。现在城市里大楼越盖越多，住宅小区也越建越漂亮。很多人都搬进楼房里去住了。我们院子里最近也搬走了五六家，明年我们家也要搬走了。
lines.pinyin: Shì. Xiànzài chéngshì li dàlóu yuè gài yuè duō, zhùzhái xiǎoqū yě yuè jiàn yuè piàoliang. Hěn duō rén dōu bān jìn lóufáng li qù zhù le. Wǒmen yuànzi li zuìjìn yě bānzǒu le wǔ liù jiā, míngnián wǒmen jiā yě yào bānzǒu le.
lines.en: Yes. More and more tall buildings are going up in the city, and housing estates are being built more and more beautifully. A lot of people have moved into apartment buildings. Five or six families in our courtyard have moved out recently; our family will move next year too.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 那太遗憾了。
lines.pinyin: Nà tài yíhàn le.
lines.en: That’s such a pity.

lines.speaker: 田芳
lines.zh: 我虽然也舍不得离开我们家的小院儿，但还是希望快点儿搬进现代化的楼房里去住。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ suīrán yě shěbude líkāi wǒmen jiā de xiǎo yuànr, dàn háishi xīwàng kuàidiǎnr bān jìn xiàndàihuà de lóufáng li qù zhù.
lines.en: Although I’m reluctant to leave our little courtyard, I still hope to move into a modern apartment building soon.

dialogues.label: 课文（二）
dialogues.headingZh: 年轻人打扮得越来越漂亮了
dialogues.headingEn: Young people are dressing more and more beautifully

lines.speaker: 王老师
lines.zh: 同学们已经学了两个多月汉语了。今天，想请大家随便谈谈自己的感想和体会，有什么意见和建议也可以提。
lines.pinyin: Tóngxuémen yǐjīng xué le liǎng ge duō yuè Hànyǔ le. Jīntiān, xiǎng qǐng dàjiā suíbiàn tántan zìjǐ de gǎnxiǎng hé tǐhuì, yǒu shénme yìjiàn hé jiànyì yě kěyǐ tí.
lines.en: You’ve already studied Chinese for over two months. Today I’d like everyone to casually share your impressions and experiences; you can also raise any opinions or suggestions.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 刚来的时候，我不习惯北京的气候，常常感冒，现在越来越习惯了。
lines.pinyin: Gāng lái de shíhou, wǒ bù xíguàn Běijīng de qìhòu, chángcháng gǎnmào, xiànzài yuèláiyuè xíguàn le.
lines.en: When I first came, I wasn’t used to Beijing’s climate and often caught colds; now I’m getting more and more used to it.

lines.speaker: 麦克
lines.zh: 我们的汉语越来越好，觉得越学越有意思了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen de Hànyǔ yuèláiyuè hǎo, juéde yuè xué yuè yǒu yìsi le.
lines.en: Our Chinese is getting better and better; the more we study, the more interesting it feels.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 我的朋友越来越多了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou yuèláiyuè duō le.
lines.en: I have more and more friends.

lines.speaker: 麦克
lines.zh: 朋友越多越好，“在家靠父母，出门靠朋友”嘛。
lines.pinyin: Péngyou yuè duō yuè hǎo, “zài jiā kào fùmǔ, chū mén kào péngyou” ma.
lines.en: The more friends the better — ‘at home rely on parents; away from home rely on friends.’

lines.speaker: 山本
lines.zh: 中国菜很好吃，我越吃越喜欢吃，所以也越来越胖了。
lines.pinyin: Zhōngguó cài hěn hǎochī, wǒ yuè chī yuè xǐhuan chī, suǒyǐ yě yuèláiyuè pàng le.
lines.en: Chinese food is delicious; the more I eat it the more I like it, so I’m also getting fatter and fatter.

lines.speaker: 麦克
lines.zh: 我觉得人们的生活一天比一天丰富，年轻人越来越会打扮，打扮得越来越漂亮了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ juéde rénmen de shēnghuó yì tiān bǐ yì tiān fēngfù, niánqīngrén yuèláiyuè huì dǎban, dǎban de yuèláiyuè piàoliang le.
lines.en: I feel people’s lives are getting richer day by day; young people are better and better at dressing up, and they’re dressing more and more beautifully.

lines.speaker: 玛丽
lines.zh: 圣诞节和新年快到了，不少商店都摆着圣诞树，装饰得非常漂亮，我看见很多中国人也买圣诞树和圣诞礼物。
lines.pinyin: Shèngdàn Jié hé xīnnián kuài dào le, bù shǎo shāngdiàn dōu bǎizhe shèngdànshù, zhuāngshì de fēicháng piàoliang, wǒ kànjian hěn duō Zhōngguó rén yě mǎi shèngdànshù hé shèngdàn lǐwù.
lines.en: Christmas and New Year are almost here; quite a few shops have Christmas trees on display, decorated very beautifully. I’ve seen many Chinese people buying Christmas trees and Christmas gifts too.

lines.speaker: 麦克
lines.zh: 老师，我听说中国过圣诞节的人越来越多了，是吗？
lines.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ tīngshuō Zhōngguó guò Shèngdàn Jié de rén yuèláiyuè duō le, shì ma?
lines.en: Teacher, I heard more and more people in China celebrate Christmas — is that true?

lines.speaker: 王老师
lines.zh: 一般家庭是不过圣诞节的。有的人过圣诞节，可能是喜欢圣诞节那种欢乐的气氛，孩子们能从爸爸妈妈那儿得到礼物，当然也很高兴。不过，中国最大的节日还是春节。
lines.pinyin: Yìbān jiātíng shì bú guò Shèngdàn Jié de. Yǒu de rén guò Shèngdàn Jié, kěnéng shì xǐhuan Shèngdàn Jié nà zhǒng huānlè de qìfēn, háizimen néng cóng bàba māma nàr dédào lǐwù, dāngrán yě hěn gāoxìng. Búguò, Zhōngguó zuì dà de jiérì háishi Chūnjié.
lines.en: Ordinary families don’t celebrate Christmas. Some people do, maybe because they like that joyous Christmas atmosphere; kids can get presents from their parents, so of course they’re happy too. But China’s biggest festival is still Spring Festival.

lines.speaker: 麦克
lines.zh: 老师，我建议，咱们开一个新年联欢会，怎么样？
lines.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ jiànyì, zánmen kāi yí ge xīnnián liánhuānhuì, zěnmeyàng?
lines.en: Teacher, I suggest we hold a New Year party — how about it?

lines.speaker: 王老师
lines.zh: 好啊！
lines.pinyin: Hǎo a!
lines.en: Great!

notes.title: 四合院儿
notes.body: Book 注释①: “四合院儿”四周由房子围成，中间是个院子。北京人过去大都住在四合院儿里. Siheyuanr is a compound of houses around a square courtyard; most Beijing residents lived in them in the past.

example.zh: 你家住的是四合院儿吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ jiā zhù de shì sìhéyuànr ma?
example.en: Does your family live in a siheyuan?

notes.title: 在家靠父母，出门靠朋友。
notes.body: Book 注释②: At home one relies on (needs the help of) one’s parents; away from home one needs friends. Spoken by 麦克 in 课文（二）.

example.zh: 朋友越多越好，“在家靠父母，出门靠朋友”嘛。
example.pinyin: Péngyou yuè duō yuè hǎo, “zài jiā kào fùmǔ, chū mén kào péngyou” ma.
example.en: The more friends the better — ‘at home rely on parents; away from home rely on friends.’

notes.title: 存现句：人或事物的存在、出现和消失
notes.body: Book 语法①. Structure: 处所词 + 动词 + 助词/补语 + 名词. Used to describe objective scenes; the object is indefinite/non-specific. Cannot say *楼上下来了王老师 — say 楼上下来了一个人.

example.zh: 前面开过来一辆出租车。
example.pinyin: Qiánmian kāi guòlái yí liàng chūzūchē.
example.en: A taxi is coming over from up ahead.

notes.title: 越来越…… 和 越……越……
notes.body: Book 语法②. 越来越……: degree changes with time (课文越来越长). 越……越……: degree changes with a condition (大楼越盖越多). 越……越…… already implies high degree — do not add 很/非常 after the second 越 (*越看越很喜欢).

example.zh: 年轻人越来越会打扮了。
example.pinyin: Niánqīngrén yuèláiyuè huì dǎban le.
example.en: Young people are better and better at dressing up.
